summary: Fisk Knob fire tower on Kent County's highest point, built 1936 at 110 ft and in use in 1939. No source found on its later fate or what stands today.

access.note: A small open park; the parking area is reached by driving less than a mile south along Algoma Avenue, according to a county high-point guide

events.note: Solon Township's history says a fire tower 110 feet high was built in 1936. A 1936 newspaper said the tower was to go up near Kent City.
Volney Thompson was towerman at the Fisk Knob fire tower in May 1939.
A fire in Walker Township, reported in May 1939, was located with help from the Fisk Knob tower and a towerman at Big Rapids.

notes_for_editor: Built 1936 and 1939 use are well sourced. Fate is unknown: a Kent County history page that reportedly covers the tower's removal returned HTTP 403 to fetch_text and could not be cited, and a Kent County facilities page also returned 403. Do not state removal without a readable source. Elevation disagrees across sources: Solon Township gives 1,075 ft, while search snippets from Kent County and WFMK give 1,072 ft; the story avoids the number. The SummitPost page is a county high-point guide, and its tower-identity remark is a guess, so it is hedged in the story. The NGS mark OK0612 is named FISK KNOB SCENIC LOT and is not treated as the tower. The Solon Township height is 110 ft, converted to 33.5 m. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the Solon page does not say the tower was on the summit, so that wording was removed; its height is not credited with the view; the Big Rapids spotter is named in the May 23, 1939 Escanaba Daily Press extract and the 1936 newspaper date (May 1, 1936) is the Oxford Leader extract on the Forest Lookouts page.
